symptom: rename/move of a microflow an agent uses as a tool left the agent naming the old microflow, and `rename … dry run` did not list the agent; mx check stayed green (ako/mxcli#2265).
cause: CustomBlobDocuments$CustomBlobDocument keeps every reference as {"documentId","qualifiedName"} inside one JSON string (Contents). RenameReferences and UpdateQualifiedNameInAllUnits match whole BSON string values, so the JSON string never equals the old name; Studio Pro re-syncs it through the agent-editor extension, which mx and mxbuild never load.
fix: For a CustomBlobDocument, rewrite each "qualifiedName" value in Contents that equals the old name or starts with it plus '.', in place (documentId, key order and indentation kept byte for byte), count it as a hit, and keep Contents out of the expression sweep so prompt text is not rewritten. Lint MPR022 reports a stored reference that resolves to nothing (refs from agent sources whose target is not in objects; System names skipped).
insight: A reference sweep over string values misses every format that nests a payload in one string — check the doc types with a JSON/XML Contents property, not only the BSON tree. The catalog already had these edges (builder_agent_refs.go), so the hit list was knowable all along; a sweep that consulted CATALOG.REFS would have caught it. Measured on 11.14.0: a dangling agent tool reference gives mx check 0 errors, so the lint rule is the only headless signal.
test: mdl/types/blob_rename_test.go; mdl/backend/modelsdk/rename_agent_2265_test.go (fails with the fix reverted: dry run lists nothing, move updates no unit); mdl/linter/rules/agent_dangling_reference_2265_test.go; live on TestApp: dry run lists SupportAgent, rename and move rewrite the tool, lint MPR022 fires only on the copy whose tool was dropped
